result.title: Learning to Verify: Signature-Guided Training for Adaptive Adversarial Detection
result.summary: Adversarial example detectors often fail when attackers explicitly attempt to bypass them. We propose a dual-model approach that keeps the original classifier fixed and trains a separate verifier to assess its predictions. During training, we identify patterns of internal neural network activations that distinguish genuine examples of each class from adversarial examples targeting that class. These patterns, called activation signatures, guide the generation of challenging adversarial examples that mislead the classifier, challenge the verifier, and internally resemble the target class. The verifier learns to recognize these examples while preserving its performance on clean inputs through knowledge distillation. At inference, the verifier evaluates the classifier's prediction without requiring activation signatures. We evaluate the approach on publicly available datasets against several adaptive attacks, including attacks unseen during training. The proposed verifier substantially outperforms directly attacked confidence-based and feature-based detectors under the evaluated L-infinity attacks. Ablation studies show that adaptive verifier training is the main source of this improvement, while signature guidance primarily benefits clean accuracy. Additional L2 evaluations reveal limitations in robustness across perturbation types.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在固定原分类器的基础上单独训练一个验证器，利用类别的内部激活「signature」生成既误导分类器、又挑战验证器且内部近似目标类的对抗样本，以提升自适应攻击下的检测鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 以独立验证器读取内部激活来判断原模型输出是否可靠，与 LVR 中核查答案是否真正依赖有效视觉证据的问题可能有共通之处，但该文限于图像分类对抗检测，迁移到多模态推理状态的可检验性需核查。
